ranking.note: Raised to P1: like #35837 it silently returns wrong data to existing callers (POST getutxos always misses), plus an unbounded allocation; same consequence class as the other P1 correctness bugs.
Raised to P2 and moved up 17: it repairs a silent semantic break of sendrawtransaction for existing third-party callers and is a stated prerequisite for wallet private broadcast.
Moved up 8: out-of-bounds reads in the JSON tokenizer used by every RPC request is the most security-adjacent item left in P3.
Moved up 7: silently disabled ZMQ leaves downstream notification consumers blind, a bigger operational hazard than the other P3 diagnostics.
Moved up 7: injecting unrelated key-origin metadata into shared PSBTs is a data-correctness and privacy leak, above the other PSBT polish items.
Moved up 7: finalizepsbt reporting complete with unusable hex misleads callers about a transaction's state.
Moved up 9: grouped with the other PSBT correctness fixes it duplicates review context with (#36343, #36332).
Moved up 6: an RPC reporting success after a partial chain rollback is a false-success bug of the same class as the ones ranked just above.
Moved down 9: valuable privacy control, but it adds modes rather than fixing wrong output, so it sits below the P3 correctness fixes.
Moved down 12: competing with #35387 on the same problem and admin-only in scope, so it ranks below the correctness fixes despite unblocking #35355.
Moved down 8: real bug but confined to the -getinfo convenience display.
Moved up 12: spurious 'Internal bug detected' responses to mining clients at shutdown is a user-visible false error, not cosmetic.
Moved up 15: setban silently dropping bans while reporting success is a false-success bug like the others grouped here.
Moved up 13: dropped HTTP responses on pipelined requests is a genuine server-side correctness race, ahead of feature additions.
Moved up 19: JSON-RPC batch replies reusing a previous element's id breaks spec expectations for every batching client.
Moved down 10: clear ergonomic win, but an optional convenience field ranks below the interface correctness fixes above.
Moved down 12: additive output field with tooling demand, but no existing caller is broken today.
Moved down 9: REST/RPC parity gap with a named consumer, still an additive feature.
Moved down 16: new aggregate statistics field with no evidence of a downstream consumer waiting on it beyond the originating issue.
Moved down 5: diagnostic message quality, below the additive fields that unblock tooling workarounds.
Moved up 9: corrects misleading analyzepsbt output (negative fee, wrong next role) for an impossible transaction.
Moved up 9: unauthenticated REST requests emitting fake disk-corruption errors misleads operators, slightly above pure interface hygiene.
Moved up 5: same deprecation-discipline class as #35433 and should be reviewed alongside it.
Moved down 8: the RPC-visible part is a refactor plus an error-code change; its payoff is in GUI drafts outside this category.
Moved up 5: same band and same problem as #34038, kept adjacent so the two approaches are compared, but second since #34038 has a dependent PR.
Moved down 15: regtest-only developer convenience with no external consumer.
Moved down 14: exploratory per-peer metric, its own card calls the value marginal and no external demand is cited.
Moved down 9: metadata for one method, benefiting code generators only.

inconsistencies: #34038 and #35387 are competing solutions to the same trace-logging problem (a reviewer on #35387 explicitly points at #34038); they must be decided together, and #34038 should be reviewed first since #35355 is built on it.

#36503 (crash on rollback without tip data) and #36266 (early failure on stale targets and concurrent runs) both harden dumptxoutset and will touch the same code; review #36503 first, it fixes a crash.
#34950 migrates generatetoaddress to self.Arg<>, which #36384 does across all RPCs; if #36384 lands, #34950 is redundant. #36167 also refactors the RPC argument helpers and will conflict with both.

#35728 and #36002 both change what GetTransaction/getrawtransaction/REST return when block data is missing or unreadable (throw vs structured candidate-hash error); their error semantics must be reconciled, #35728 first as the base behaviour change.

#36200 and #36204 both address resource exhaustion of the HTTP server's fixed worker/connection pool; review #36200 first (trivially triggerable, removes a deliberate sleep), then #36204 for the slowloris case.

#36332, #36343, #36567 and #36569 are four independent PSBT correctness fixes touching overlapping RPCs (descriptorprocesspsbt, finalizepsbt, joinpsbts, analyzepsbt); reviewing them as one batch avoids repeated context and likely conflicts.
#35433 and #36488 are both scheduled RPC argument deprecations gated on -deprecatedrpc; they should follow one consistent deprecation pattern and be reviewed together.

#33117 refactors the loadtxoutset RPC while #36503/#36266 change dumptxoutset; all three touch the assumeutxo RPC surface and change returned error codes, which is a compatibility concern worth coordinating.
result.notes: The band distribution is deliberately spread: three P1s are interface-level security or wrong-data-returned problems (credential exposure, silently incomplete scanblocks results, a REST endpoint that always misses); P2 holds DoS/crash/leak fixes and the three feature gaps with documented external demand (unix sockets, testsubmitpackage, script history). The large P3 group is ordered correctness-first, then additive fields and parity gaps, then interface hygiene and tests, per the category's compatibility-first ordering. Only three bands moved; everything else keeps its original band.
